summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and ran all six tasks in plan.md. Each task got an implementer subagent and a review subagent, and a "Final whole-branch code review" agent was dispatched. Both soak tests passed (240 s and 720 s). `sdd-state finish` ran and published a receipt. After I answered its finish-option question, the agent merged by fast-forward into main. It stopped once while the plan was unfinished, and that stop was the finish-option question. I never had to send "continue".
reasoning: Every criterion is backed by the session log and git. The skill loaded before any work, all six tasks were implemented and reviewed, and the final review agent was dispatched. sdd-state finish returned status=finished with a receipt path. Main holds all the commits, and the soak files are unchanged since the initial commit. The only stop came after finish had run: the finishing skill's merge question, which my script allowed me to answer. The agent kept its turn alive through both soak runs without needing "continue".

observations.description: On startup Claude Code offered 'Newer Opus model available ... Update settings to use Opus 5.5? Claude Code will restart', even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the header then showed Opus 5.5. It's confusing that the prompt appears at all.

Before any work started, the agent asked about the spec location: 'The decision-record tool refuses design.md because the spec must sit in a subdirectory'. A root-level design.md is a normal layout, so the tool turned it into a question for the user. I answered 'go ahead with what the plan says', and decision records were skipped as a result.

Four commit subjects have the trailer stuck onto the subject line, e.g. 'feat: add token bucket limiter Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>'. The Haiku implementer subagents wrote the trailer badly. The agent noticed this and left it in place.

The final review summary reports a floating-point edge case in the simulate CLI: '--limit 1 --calls 11' gives allowed=1 where exact arithmetic gives allowed=2. It also reports that a negative --calls value gives a negative denied count. The agent left both as is because the plan says so.

The 600 s Bash timeout pushed the long soak command into the background ('Command did not complete within its 600s timeout and was moved to the background'). The agent handled it with tracked-job wait, and the turn stayed alive.
There is no .gitignore, so __pycache__ directories are left untracked after the run.
The agent ran `git pull` during the merge even though there is no remote. It printed a 'There is no tracking information' warning, which was harmless.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before implementation work
criteria.evidence: Screen after my first prompt: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". This came before any Agent dispatch. The session log has '"skill":"hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development"' twice.

criteria.criterion: All tasks completed, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on main checkout
criteria.evidence: Agent descriptions in the session log run from 'Implement Task 1: Package and clocks' through 'Review Task 6 (spec + quality)', followed by 'Final whole-branch code review'. `git log` on main shows f3bd457, b463982, 860d0ac, 699a192, e227035 and ed628d4 above 1199cab (initial). `git branch` shows '* main', and the ratelimit branch was deleted after the merge. A tool result shows that finish ran: 'status=finished ... receipt=.../home/.cache/hyperpowers/receipts/plan-76cc6a12-20261106T050305Z'. The agent's final message: 'ratelimit is merged into main locally, and all 27 unit tests pass'.

`git log --oneline --all -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py` returns only '1199cab initial: design, plan and soak tests'. A diff from the root commit to HEAD on those paths is empty. `git status` shows only the untracked __pycache__ directories. The agent also said: 'Neither soak test file was changed.'

STOP: "Which option?" | question. This was the finish menu (merge / PR / keep), shown after finish had published its receipt but before the merge. I answered 'merge back to main locally'. Nothing else counts as a stop. The upfront questions (workspace, DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS, spec path) were AskUserQuestion dialogs before Task 1 started. After that the spinner stayed on through all six tasks and the 12-minute soak, and I never needed to send 'continue'.
